newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Investment in Cambodia tops $360m through April.
newsitem.headline: Investment in Cambodia tops $360m through April.

text.p: Private investment in Cambodia totalled $360.3 million in the first four months of this year, more than double the same period in 1996, the state investment board said on Tuesday.
The growth was mainly driven by the approval late last year of U.S. Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade status for Cambodia, officials at the Cambodian Investment Board (CIB) said.
MFN lowered duties on Cambodian exports to the levels of most U.S. trading partners and consequently attracted many garment manufacturers, said CIB representative Chea Vuthy.
A CIB report released on Tuesday said half of all investments approved between January and April 1996 were garment manufacturing projects.
The CIB approved 32 garment factories worth nearly $30 million, the report said.
South Korea was the leading investor nation and had the largest single approved project -- a $200 million cement factory to be built by Korean firm Tong Yang Corp, the report said.

Other major projects included a $50 million planned industrial park to be developed by Sun Wah Ltd of Hong Kong and a $38 million wireless phone system to be developed by Portacom Wireless Communication Inc of the United States, the report said.
A dozen agroindustrial projects, including bean, corn, sesame, cassava and banana growing and processing were also approved, according to the CIB.
The total value of approved projects for the first four months of 1996 was $175 million compared to $360.3 for January through April 1997, Chea Vuthy told Reuters.
The CIB is the investment arm of the Cambodian government and is charged with approving all major private sector applications.
It handles foreign and Cambodian projects. Most applications are made by foreigners, though many companies have local partners, officials said.
